news.originalContent:
Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed accidentally made the best case for why parents should and do shelter their children.

The 2026 midterm election cycle isn’t necessarily being fought on the culture-war battlefield. Still, some candidates, like El-Sayed, find themselves there. 60 Minutes host Ross Douthat sat down with El-Sayed on Oct. 22 at Wayne State University. The two discussed his campaign and potential policies should he beat Republican Mike Rogers in November.

During the interview, El-Sayed was asked how he squares his self-professed pro-Constitution, pro-individual rights views with issues like transgender athletes. His answer was telling, as it exposed a fundamental reason protective parents shield their children from technology.

Douthat: “What about the rights, what about the rights of parents to control over their children’s education? Because a lot of places where there’s tension between Islam and Muslim voters and what I’m calling cultural liberalism are around issues like what is taught in school? What happens with transgender kids on sports teams and so on, right? Like, these are places where rights are in conflict, right? What do you think happens there?”

El-Sayed: “The whole world, all the world’s information in your pocket. The notion somehow that you are going to prevent your child from being exposed to something that you may find disagreeable, and that that is going to be because of school, is so profoundly outdated because, of course, you have all the information and they have all the information. So here’s the thing about it. I think it’s really important for us to recognize that the free flow of information is actually a beautiful thing. It’s really important, and the most important thing you can do is not try to protect a person from seeing a thing. It’s about trying to make sure that as you coach your kid through the world that you are engaging with them and saying, ‘Here’s what I believe. Here’s what you may see in the world. You get to make your choices about who you’re going to be in the world.’ But that’s going to require us to make do with the fact that, like, the internet is a real thing.”

Is El-Sayed really arguing that parents should never try to protect children from anything because the internet exists? In theory, this would mean hardcore, violent porn and videos of suicide and murder. He and his supporters would likely object, claiming that these materials are not the same as exposing your children to transgender ideology. Still, the question he seemingly can’t answer is: Who gets to decide where the line is drawn? (Sign up for Mary Rooke’s weekly newsletter here!)

The internet is real, as El-Sayed pointed out. It is the largest source of information, our modern-day Library of Alexandria, just more depraved. However, acknowledging this does not mean parents must give their children access. Parents have a responsibility to do the opposite because protecting their innocence and bolstering their understanding of their family’s moral code before they are inundated with harmful ideologies is critical to their development and to their connection to their family legacy.

He’s essentially arguing that parents shouldn’t protect their daughters from, say, seeing male genitals in their bathrooms or being paralyzed by a biological male on an opposing team because they have phones in their pockets that expose them to much worse. It’s almost as if it never occurred to him that parents prohibit or restrict technology use with their children because they are trying to protect them from all these evils.

El-Sayed’s answer validates the very parental instincts he calls “profoundly outdated.” The parents who limit screen time, reject transgender ideology, and insist on sex-based categories in sports, locker rooms, and bathrooms are not in denial about the internet and are far more likely to be the same parents refusing to provide their children with a phone. They understand that unrestricted internet access does not produce wiser, freer children who are happy and well-adjusted. They see how earlier exposure to pornography, self-harm content, and radical ideologies destroys a child’s sense of wonder and safety. (RELATED: The Cream Of The Crop Exam For College Entry Nothing Like It Used To Be. Study Shows Test-Makers Neutered It)

By making the idiotic argument that school-based protections are pointless because phones exist, El-Sayed inadvertently concedes that the modern digital environment for children is hostile to childhood. As much as he’d like to claim that this is about safeguarding rights, he’s really making a false moral claim that parents have no authority to set boundaries. And the more chaotic and explicit our culture becomes, the more essential it is that parents reject him and retain the final say.

If parents were on the fence about whether their children should have a phone in their pocket, El-Sayed just made the best case for holding off.

Amid nationwide outcry over data centers, OpenAI said Monday it will use less electricity at a new data center campus when the power grid is strained.

The Sam Altman-run AI giant said it plans to turn down the juice during extreme weather or emergencies at its planned data center site in Effingham County, Georgia — where locals protested the $30 billion project over the summer.

The sprawling data center campus outside of Savannah will need an estimated 3.2 gigawatts of power, according to OpenAI. It’s expected to launch in 2028.

Under its “Grid Protectors Program” OpenAI will cut up to 1 gigawatt enough to power about 700,000 homes — to help stabilize the local grid as needed, the company said.

“Our ambition is to make this kind of flexibility a core part of how we build and operate future campuses,” OpenAI said in a statement.

“That means designing facilities to reduce electricity use when needed and working with utilities to agree on how much demand can be reduced, how quickly and for how long.”

OpenAI also said it would “work with grid operators to supply power from on-site generation or storage, and use batteries and power controls to smooth changes in demand.”

Georgia Power appeared to welcome the policy.

“We appreciate the leadership and thoughtfulness of the OpenAI team as they prepare to bring significant investment and cutting-edge technology to Georgia,” said Aaron Mitchell, a senior VP of for the utility.

“At Georgia Power, we are working every day to help ensure that growth from data centers and other large-energy users brings value for our customers through higher reliability and lower prices,” Mitchell said in a statement back in July.

Effingham County is the only data center campus OpenAI has planned to launch on its own to date. It runs 28 data center facilities nationwide, according to Baxtel, a data center research platform. It’s also working on a campus in partnership with Oracle in Wisconsin.

Companies, federal agencies, and state leaders have been trying to find ways to make data centers more flexible, Reuters noted. The ability for centers to shift use of electricity could save $40 billion to $150 billion in capital investments over the next decade, according to a Duke University study.

“Demand response can materially soften peak impacts,” Alexander Kheder, an analyst with BMI, a multinational research firm, told Reuters. “But scaling curtailment agreements across hundreds of new facilities will demand significant capital expenditure and coordinated policy frameworks.”

Still, public opinion has soured on data centers.

People would rather see a nuclear power plant built in their neighborhood than a data center, a May Gallup poll found, with a whopping 71% of Americans opposed to the latter.
news.content:
پوشش ما را بیشتر در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. در میان اعتراض سراسری نسبت به مراکز داده، OpenAI روز دوشنبه گفت که از برق کمتری در پردیس مرکز داده جدید استفاده خواهد کرد، زمانی که شبکه برق دچار مشکل شود. غول هوش مصنوعی سام آلتمن گفت که قصد دارد در هنگام آب و هوای شدید یا شرایط اضطراری در سایت مرکز داده برنامه ریزی شده خود در Effingham County اعتراض کردند. طبق گفته OpenAI، پردیس گسترده مرکز داده در خارج از ساوانا به 3.2 گیگاوات برق نیاز دارد. انتظار می‌رود که در سال 2028 راه‌اندازی شود. طبق گفته شرکت OpenAI تحت "برنامه محافظ شبکه" خود تا 1 گیگاوات برق مصرفی حدود 700000 خانه را کاهش می‌دهد - تا در صورت لزوم به تثبیت شبکه محلی کمک کند. OpenAI در بیانیه‌ای گفت: «جاه‌طلبی ما این است که این نوع انعطاف‌پذیری را به بخشی اصلی از نحوه ساخت و راه‌اندازی پردیس‌های آینده تبدیل کنیم.» این به معنای طراحی تسهیلات برای کاهش مصرف برق در صورت نیاز و همکاری با شرکت‌های خدمات شهری برای توافق در مورد میزان تقاضا، سرعت و مدت زمان کاهش است. OpenAI همچنین گفت که "با اپراتورهای شبکه برای تامین برق از تولید یا ذخیره سازی در محل کار خواهد کرد و از باتری ها و کنترل های برق برای هموارسازی تغییرات تقاضا استفاده خواهد کرد."
به نظر می‌رسد جورجیا پاور از این سیاست استقبال می‌کند. آرون میچل، معاون ارشد این شرکت، گفت: «ما از رهبری و اندیشمندی تیم OpenAI در حالی که آماده می‌شوند سرمایه‌گذاری قابل توجه و فناوری‌های پیشرفته را به گرجستان وارد کنند، قدردانی می‌کنیم.»

There are colorful houses in Los Angeles. There are neutral houses — and Neutra houses — in Los Angeles. And then there’s this one.

Sitting proudly atop Mount Royal Drive in the aging-hipster enclave of Eagle Rock is a 138-year-old Queen Anne Victorian painted head to toe in unapologetic purple. And lavender. And mauve. With a dash of cotton-candy pink and a smattering of seafoam, Fanta orange and terracotta.

Locals call the property Esperanza — Spanish for “hope.” Seeing as it just hit the market for $2 million, ordinary local house hunters can only “hope” to get their dainty gloves on this vintage showstopper.

Built in 1888 right before the collapse of the Southern California land boom, the house is pure Victorian pomp and grace.

Think a witch’s hat turret, a wealth of spectacular chandeliers, decorative scalloped shingles, a wide covered porch framed by stone (perfect for judging passers-by “To Kill a Mockingbird” style), a separate secret balcony accessible by a sexy spiral staircase, and that impossible-to-ignore lavender exterior framed in bright-pink and dark-purple trim.

It looks like something a fairy-tale pixie hopped up on grape soda might have dreamed up.

A post shared by Laurie Turner | Pasadena Real Estate Agent (@laurieturnersellspasadena)

The generous 2,670-square-foot home boasts four bedrooms and three bathrooms on a nearly half-acre lot — with “city light” views.

Inside, classical details stand the test of time — wood floors throughout, a dramatic living-room fireplace, and that respectable all-bedrooms-up layout.

The kitchen, primary suite and bathrooms have been blessed with more recent upgrades, but the theme of purple royalty remains strong throughout, including the kitchen island.

Speaking of bathrooms, those grandiose bathtubs are fit for a “Game of Thrones” king, complete with an elaborate dragon faucet in one.

There’s even an in-ground pool out back for further floating and emoting.

The last known owner Leonora Pierotti, who was said to be born in 1913, was the daughter of Italian immigrant Attilio Pierotti, who made his fortune in California spearheading the packing and shipment of local fruits, including citrus.

Leonora Pierotti was no casual fan of the color purple, apparently. According to listing agent Laurie Turner, Pierotti, who reportedly drove a purple Hummer, “had a penchant for purple and it made her happy.”

Eagle Rock has spent the last two decades metamorphosing from suburban to sought-after, and this house sits right in the middle of that creative renaissance — close enough to the artsy coffee shops and new restaurants, far enough up that hill to feel like its own little kingdom of all it surveys.

For $2 million you get more than square footage and ample gardens.

You get a genuine piece of Industrial Revolution-era LA that somehow survived the wrecking ball, the stucco-fication of the City of Angels, and every flash-in-the-pan design trend that tried to wipe out this kind of joyful maximalism.

Esperanza is currently listed with Coldwell Banker Realty.

news.content: بیشتر پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. خانه های رنگارنگی در لس آنجلس وجود دارد. خانه های خنثی - و خانه های نوترا - در لس آنجلس وجود دارد. و سپس این یکی وجود دارد. ملکه آن ویکتوریایی 138 ساله که با افتخار بر فراز کوه رویال درایو در منطقه قدیمی ایگل راک نشسته است، سر تا پا را به رنگ ارغوانی غیرقابل تأسف کشیده است. و اسطوخودوس. و ارغوانی. با رنگ صورتی پنبه ای و کمی کف دریایی، نارنجی فانتا و سفالی. مردم محلی این ملک را اسپرانزا - اسپانیایی به معنای "امید" می نامند. شکارچیان معمولی خانه‌های محلی با دیدن این که به تازگی با قیمت 2 میلیون دلار وارد بازار شده‌اند، فقط می‌توانند «امید داشته باشند» که دستکش‌های زیبای خود را در این نمایشگاه قدیمی به دست آورند. بزرگترین اخبار، نظر و فرهنگ شکل‌دهنده کالیفرنیا در حال حاضر. لطفاً یک ایمیل معتبر ارائه دهید. با کلیک کردن بر روی بالا، با شرایط استفاده و سیاست حفظ حریم خصوصی موافقت می کنید. این خانه درست قبل از فروپاشی رونق زمین در کالیفرنیای جنوبی در سال 1888 ساخته شد، این خانه شکوه و ظرافت خالص ویکتوریایی است. به برجک کلاه جادوگر، انبوهی از لوسترهای دیدنی، زوناهای قلابدار تزیینی، یک ایوان وسیع سرپوشیده با قاب سنگ (مناسب برای قضاوت رهگذران به سبک «کشتن مرغ مقلد»)، یک بالکن مخفی مجزا که با یک راه پله مارپیچ سکسی قابل دسترسی است، و قاب بیرونی روشن و غیرممکن است، فکر کنید. تزئینات بنفش تیره. به نظر می رسد چیزی است که یک پیکسی افسانه ای روی نوشابه انگور پریده است. پست به اشتراک گذاشته شده توسط Laurie Turner | نماینده املاک پاسادنا (@laurieturnersellspasadena)

Photo by Mandel NGAN / AFP via Getty Images

OpenAI’s top lobbyist is trying to shape the way 2028’s top political contenders think about artificial intelligence, Politico reported Monday.

Chris Lehane, OpenAI’s top lobbyist, circulated sent a memo to top presidential candidates, arguing that candidates need to give voters a positive policy platform for AI, rather than just messaging about opposing data centers, according to Politico. The memo is reportedly being circulated as a way for these presidential hopefuls to consider policies ranging from tax policies, how AI can make life more affordable and how to beat China in the AI race.

“No historical analogy is perfect (thankfully, we’re not in a depression!), but 2028 has echoes of 1932: candidates must earn the trust of Americans who feel increasingly powerless in the face of disruptive technologies, powerful financial interests, accelerating change, and the erosion of institutions that once anchored daily life,” the memo, which was obtained by Politico, stated. “AI threatens to compound that anxiety through a transformation whose consequences no one can fully predict. It is a general purpose technology on the scale of the wheel, the printing press, and electricity.”

OpenAI sent the memo to roughly six prospective presidential candidates as well as some lawmakers and notable political operatives, a person with knowledge of the memo told the outlet, speaking on condition of anonymity to discuss private conversations.

OpenAI did not respond to a request for comment.

Instead, Lehane called for a “third path” between pursuing AI without “speed limits” and those who would “keep control over the technology in the hands of a self-appointed elite,” per the memo.

He said that one-fifth of the ads Democrats aired in the midterm elections attacking data centers are concentrated in Michigan, Texas, Ohio and Pennsylvania, where many of the data centers being built, adding that Democrats may not be able to provide the “answer 2028 voters are looking for” based on their anti-data center midterm messaging. (RELATED: Why Does Big Tech Have All Eyes On Big Race In Middle America?)

Lehane, a Democratic operative and former press secretary to then-Vice President Al Gore, charged that if America loses its lead against China in the AI race, this could be the “2028 version of the 2002 vote to go to war in Iraq.”

The memo called for advancing tax policy that would help Americans benefit from the “upside” of the AI boom, protecting children while expanding opportunity and ensuring that AI can help make life more affordable for Americans.

“The successful candidates won’t promise to stop the future or simply trust everything will work out. They’ll show Americans how to shape that future and benefit from it,” the memo concluded.

OpenAI Told Trump They’d "Rebuild" American Manufacturing… Here’s What They Were ACTUALLY Doing https://t.co/Pa84pj7f0D

The memo to presidential contenders follows reports that OpenAI will launch a policy and public relations campaign after the midterm elections, according to Axios. As part of that effort, the company will rebrand data centers as “AI compute campuses,” per the outlet.

Americans have grown hostile to data centers in recent months, with nearly half of Americans saying the projects would increase home costs, according to a late September Pew Research poll.

“You can try to chase the moment, or seek to inform the moment via the power of ideas,” Lehane told the outlet.

The company will lobby Congress about AI “speed limits” to ensure that “people should have more control” over how AI shapes their lives, Lehane told Axios.

The AI industry seeks to increase its relationship with Democrats as the party remains poised for a sweep that may give them control of the House and potentially the Senate, according to the latest Cook Political Report. Meta continues its bipartisan lobbyist team, according to Axios.
news.content:
عکس از ماندل NGAN / خبرگزاری فرانسه از طریق گتی ایماژ
پولیتیکو روز دوشنبه گزارش داد که لابی‌گر ارشد OpenAI در تلاش است تا طرز فکر رقبای سیاسی برتر سال 2028 را در مورد هوش مصنوعی شکل دهد. کریس لیهان، لابی‌گر ارشد OpenAI، یادداشتی را برای نامزدهای ارشد ریاست‌جمهوری ارسال کرد و استدلال کرد که نامزدها باید به رای‌دهندگان یک پلتفرم سیاست مثبت برای هوش مصنوعی بدهند، نه اینکه صرفاً به مراکز داده در مورد مخالفت‌ها پیام بدهند. گزارش شده است که این یادداشت به‌عنوان راهی برای این نامزدهای ریاست‌جمهوری منتشر می‌شود تا سیاست‌هایی از سیاست‌های مالیاتی، اینکه چگونه هوش مصنوعی می‌تواند زندگی را مقرون به صرفه‌تر کند و چگونه چین را در مسابقه هوش مصنوعی در نظر بگیرد، منتشر می‌شود. در این یادداشت که پولیتیکو به دست آورده است، آمده است: کاندیداها باید اعتماد آمریکایی‌هایی را که در مقابل فناوری‌های مخرب، منافع مالی قدرتمند، تغییرات شتاب‌دهنده، و فرسایش نهادهایی که زمانی زندگی روزمره را تثبیت می‌کردند، احساس ناتوانی فزاینده‌ای می‌کنند، جلب کنند. این یک فناوری همه منظوره در مقیاس چرخ، ماشین چاپ و برق است.
فردی که از این یادداشت مطلع بود به این رسانه گفت که OpenAI این یادداشت را برای تقریباً شش نامزد احتمالی ریاست جمهوری و همچنین برخی از قانونگذاران و فعالان سیاسی قابل توجه ارسال کرد و به شرط ناشناس ماندن در مورد گفتگوهای خصوصی صحبت کرد.

WASHINGTON — The outcome of races for 10 House Republican incumbents will determine whether the lower chamber falls to Democrats in the 2026 midterm elections.

All the GOP lawmakers have expressed confidence in their re-election despite the historic headwinds their party faces and President Trump’s growing unpopularity.

But several have also survived tough matchups in the past and are counting on their legislative record to help them defend the GOP’s 218-214 majority in the House.

Hudson Valley Rep. Mike Lawler was first elected to Congress in 2022 as one of several New York Republicans who helped deliver them the House during former President Joe Biden’s presidency.

His reelection would be a big step to keeping GOP control of the House under Trump.

Lawler, 40, opted against a run for governor in his state and has consistently touted himself as one of the most bipartisan members of the lower chamber and as a Republican who is willing to break publicly with the president on health care, tax and immigration issues.

The latest poll shows Lawler and his opponent, Cait Conley, an Army combat veteran and ex-Biden administration official, in a statistical tie.

The Michigan Republican is serving his first term in the House after winning election to a seat left vacant by then-Rep. Elissa Slotkin, who triumphed in her 2024 Senate race.

Some polls have shown Barrett, an Army helicopter pilot and Iraq war veteran, beating his Democratic opponent this cycle, William Lawrence, a self-described democratic socialist who’s drawn scrutiny for eyebrow-raising remarks wishing death on a centrist lawmaker.

Kiggans was one of several House Republicans whose seat was threatened through a redistricting effort pushed by Virginia Democrats that was eventually struck down by the courts.

But surveys are still showing her tied or in a statistical tie with Democrat Elaine Luria, who previously lost the seat in Virginia’s Second District to Kiggans in 2022.

Ohio Rep. Max Miller is headed into the toughest re-election race of his time in the House after a much-publicized divorce from Emily Moreno, the daughter of Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio), and a subsequent custody battle dredged up details about his alleged physical abuse.

The Republican pol has denied accusations of abuse from his former spouse and even leveled the same charge at her.

Miller’s challenger, Brian Poindexter, has also been surging in some surveys — despite the 7th District being historically Republican since the 1930s.

The Texas GOPer is trailing political newcomer and Latin Grammy-winning artist Bobby Pulido in most polls, even as the Democrat has faced tough questions about performing alongside a registered sex offender in his band.

De La Cruz first won election in the Lone Star State’s 15th District in 2022 and was re-elected in 2024.

A Republican-led, mid-decade redistricting in Texas last year didn’t appear to give her a greater advantage.

House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) has publicly rejected polling showing that Van Orden is in trouble in Wisconsin, claiming that Republican voters are being undercounted.

The few surveys conducted have only had Democratic sponsors, lending credence to the speaker’s theory.

The Wisconsin Republican is in a rematch race against Democrat Rebecca Cooke, a small business owner he defeated by more than 11,000 votes in 2024.

The latest surveys show Perry in a dead heat with Democrat Janelle Stelson in Pennsylvania’s 10th District — in another rematch race from 2024.

It’s the most difficult re-election Perry has faced since he began serving in the House in 2013, though Republicans’ shellacking in the 2018 midterms comes close.

Internal polls aligned with Evans’ re-election effort have put him in either a statistical tie or dead even race against Democrat Manny Rutinel.

The Colorado Republican unseated Rep. Yadira Caraveo (D-Colo.) in 2024.

Valadao will offer the first of whether a Democrat-led redistricting effort in California successfully took a handful of GOP seats out of competition for the House.

After handily winning re-election in 2024, the Republican rep is facing Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.)-backed Randy Villegas in the Golden State’s 22nd District.

Even some GOP-aligned polls are showing Ciscomani headed for defeat on Election Day against Democrat and Marine veteran JoAnna Mendoza.

Ciscomani was one of several Republicans elected in 2022 who delivered their party the House.
news.content: پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود بیشتر ببینید. واشنگتن - نتیجه رقابت‌ها برای 10 نماینده جمهوری‌خواه مجلس نمایندگان آمریکا تعیین می‌کند که آیا مجلس پایین به دست دموکرات‌ها در انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای 2026 می‌افتد یا خیر. همه قانون‌گذاران حزب جمهوری‌خواه علی‌رغم مشکلات تاریخی که حزبشان با آن مواجه است و رشد غیرمحبوب رئیس‌جمهور ترامپ، به انتخاب مجدد خود ابراز اطمینان کرده‌اند. اما چندین نفر نیز در گذشته از رقابت‌های سخت جان سالم به در برده‌اند و روی سوابق قانونی خود حساب می‌کنند تا به آنها کمک کند تا از اکثریت 218 بر 214 حزب جمهوری‌خواه دفاع کنند. مایک لاولر، نماینده دره هادسون، برای اولین بار در سال 2022 به عنوان یکی از چندین جمهوری‌خواه نیویورک به کنگره انتخاب شد. مجلس در زمان ترامپ لاولر، 40 ساله، مخالف نامزدی برای فرمانداری در ایالت خود بود و پیوسته خود را به عنوان یکی از دو حزبی ترین اعضای اتاق پایین و جمهوری خواه معرفی می کرد که مایل است به طور علنی با رئیس جمهور در زمینه مراقبت های بهداشتی، مالیاتی و مسائل مهاجرت در هم شکسته شود. آخرین نظرسنجی نشان می دهد که لالر و رقیبش، کیت کانلی، یک مقام نظامی کهنه کار ارتش و یکی از اعضای سابق ارتش. جمهوری خواه میشیگان پس از پیروزی در انتخابات برای یک کرسی خالی که نماینده وقت مجلس نمایندگان آن زمان خالی مانده بود، اولین دوره خود را در مجلس می گذراند. الیسا اسلاتکین، که در رقابت‌های سنا در سال 2024 پیروز شد. برخی نظرسنجی‌ها نشان می‌دهند که بارت، خلبان هلیکوپتر ارتش و کهنه سرباز جنگ عراق، دموی خود را شکست داده است.

A West Point cadet fed his pregnant girlfriend a sedative-laced smoothie and “shoved abortion pills” into her vagina, killing the fetus — then enrolled in Columbia University’s public-health masters program, a new lawsuit says.

Disgraced former army cadet Caleb T. Suh — the son of US Department of Veterans Chief of Staff Dr. Ryung Suh — already admitted in federal court that he deliberately tricked his then-girlfriend into chugging what he assured her was a “special pregnancy protein powder” shake in 2022, according to the lawsuit and his guilty plea.

The sick smoothie was actually chockful of the sedatives Xanax and Promethazine.

The ailing woman, also a cadet, was overcome with drowsiness, and that’s when “Suh shoved abortion pills into Ms. Doe’s vagina and in her mouth,” according to the suit.

The woman went on to lose the baby she had hoped to keep — while Suh ended up studying emergency medicine at Cornell University in upstate New York and received a bachelor’s degree from the Ivy League school in 2024, court documents said.

The defendant was eventually charged in the disturbing case this past spring and pleaded guilty to felony assault in June — repped by lawyer Thomas Kenniff, who previously defended infamous deadly Manhattan subway vigilante Daniel Penny. He is awaiting sentencing.

Suh then enrolled in the prestigious master’s program at Ivy League Columbia in Manhattan, the suit said.

A source with knowledge of the situation said Columbia was unaware of Suh’s criminal conviction before the media recently began inquiring about his case, noting that applications do not ask for disclosures of criminality.

The source said that after learning of Suh’s past, the school “took swift action” — but did not specify what that meant.

“For years, Ms. Doe has been forced to grapple with her experience,” the lawsuit said. “Ms. Doe’s life has been irreparably changed, and she has lost a baby that she intended to keep.

“Meanwhile, Defendant Suh matriculated at Cornell University, earned a Bachelor’s degree, and is now enrolled at Columbia University.”

It is unclear whether either Suh or the woman — both of whom would be in their 20s — ever graduated from West Point.

The pair had started dating while enrolled at West Point in 2020, with the anonymous woman discovering she was pregnant in 2022, the suit claimed.

While she wanted to keep the pregnancy, Suh was staunchly opposed and “even threatened to commit suicide if she did not terminate the pregnancy,” the suit said.

Suh then began feigning support for her and the baby — even as he obtained the abortion pills by stealing her identity and opening a fake account with an online pharmacy, ordering the drugs in her name and having them shipped to West Point, according to his plea and the suit.

“I also obtained Xanax through a friend,” Suh admitted in his guilty plea. “My intent was [to] use the Xanax to unwittingly sedate my girlfriend so that I could then administer the abortion pills, which I had obtained via the online pharmacy.”

He even asked questions on the pharmacy’s online forum, including “[W]ill I feel the pills in my vaginia?”

Suh eventually gave the pregnant young woman what he called a “special pregnancy protein powder” laced with the sedatives, the suit said. It’s unclear how far along she was in the pregnancy at the time.

Despite the woman’s revulsion at the taste of the drink, Suh insisted she finish it, “holding the bottle against her lips and forcing her to drink it,” according to court papers.

She spent the next few hours sick and incapacitated, floating in and out of consciousness.

At some point, she recalled Suh “began touching her vagina,” the suit claimed.

She also remembered finding two pills in her mouth and spat them out, but Suh shoved them back in, the filing said.

“Eat this,” Suh allegedly urged her. “It’s good for you.”

When she awoke, the young woman discovered she was “profusely bleeding from her vagina,” according to the suit, and, fearing a miscarriage, tried to call Suh, but he didn’t answer.

The woman called 911, and doctors confirmed she was suffering a miscarriage, and she was given a D&C to remove the fetus’s remains, her suit said.

But Suh, still ignoring calls from the woman he drugged, was worried about being discovered and continued posting on the pharmacy forums about what to do if the doctors “see the remaining pills” in her vagina, the lawsuit said.

The two broke up soon after and Suh went on to finish his undergraduate degree at Cornell, enrolling the fall of 2024 — the same semester where a horrific frat house gang rape allegedly occurred — and began studying emergency medicine, claiming his long-term goal was to “become a physician leader committed to advancing both patient care and structural equity.”

His former girlfriend’s lawyer, Russell Kornblith, said in a statement, “As a parent it is difficult not to be incredibly emotionally drained by thinking about what our client has experienced both by the loss of a pregnancy she intended to keep and being robbed of autonomy over her own body.”

His client is allowed to remain anonymous at least for now — which is typical for sex accusers — but a judge could decide down the road to make her name  public if the defendant successfully makes a case for it.

Suh was charged in Manhattan Federal Court, before his first semester at Columbia, and pled guilty in June.

Several weeks ago, he asked to delay his sentencing until January, so he could finish his semester without interruption.

The request was granted, and prosecutors are seeking two years behind bars.
news.content: در نتایج جستجوی خود بیشتر از پوشش ما دیدن کنید. یک دعوای حقوقی جدید می گوید که یک دانشجوی دانشگاه وست پوینت به دوست دختر باردار خود یک اسموتی آرام بخش خورد و "قرص های سقط جنین" را به واژن او زد و جنین را کشت - سپس در برنامه کارشناسی ارشد بهداشت عمومی دانشگاه کلمبیا ثبت نام کرد، یک دعوی قضایی جدید می گوید. ریونگ سو - قبلاً در دادگاه فدرال اعتراف کرده بود که عمداً دوست دختر خود را فریب داده است تا در سال 2022 با توجه به دادخواست و ادعای گناه خود، چیزی را که به او اطمینان داده بود یک شیک «پودر پروتئین حاملگی ویژه» است ببرد. اسموتی بیمار در واقع مملو از داروهای آرام بخش، Xanecom، زناکس و پرومتها بود. خواب‌آلودگی، و این زمانی بود که «سو قرص‌های سقط جنین را به خانم هل داد. طبق دادخواست، زن در ادامه فرزند خود را از دست داد - در حالی که سو به تحصیل در رشته پزشکی اورژانس در دانشگاه کورنل در شمال ایالت نیویورک پرداخت و مدرک لیسانس خود را از مدرسه آیوی لیگ در سال 2024 دریافت کرد. متهم سرانجام در بهار گذشته در پرونده نگران‌کننده‌ای متهم شد و در ماه ژوئن به جرم جنایت خود اعتراف کرد - وکیل توماس کنیف که قبلاً از دنیل پنی، مراقب بدنام متروی منهتن دفاع می‌کرد. او در انتظار صدور حکم است. سوخ سپس در برنامه معتبر کارشناسی ارشد در آیوی لیگ کلمبیا در منهتن ثبت نام کرد. یک منبع آگاه

Darren Till is irate that he didn’t get the Jake Paul fight.

After loads of speculation and even alleged confirmation from Most Valuable Promotions CEO Nakisa Bidarian that he was in the running to be Paul’s next opponent, Till unloaded after being passed over for the fight in an interview with Ariel Helwani.

“We agreed on a price and obviously it was going to be in Dubai on the 24th of December, where I live,” Till said. “I’ve been in camp for the past two weeks with my coach; I flew him out. Getting ready seven weeks away… Out of nowhere, this fight gets announced; this daft fight gets announced with Cédric Doumbé.”

Doumbé and Paul are scheduled to fight on Christmas Eve in Dubai at cruiserweight (200 pounds), though Doumbé, who hasn’t boxed since 2015 but is a decorated kickboxer, last fought 30 months ago at 175 pounds.

“I don’t think anyone outside of his own house knows who he is,” Till explained. “Jake probably just wants to see how his jaw is against someone who weighs 150 pounds on a good day. It’s a fraudulent showing. Everyone is a fraud. Jake’s a fraud. Nakisa is a little fraud. Waste of my time. Couldn’t give a f–k. If you want to fight me next year, fight me next year. So I just wasted about 5,000 pounds getting my coach out here, but it’s all good.”

Doumbé is 5-foot-8 with a 73-inch reach, while Paul measures 6-foot-1 with a 76-inch reach.

“Cédric Doumbé weighs 170 pounds,” Till explained. “Jake Paul’s 220 pounds. Are we all just going to buy into this fight because he’s clever at marketing and stuff like that… What kind of fight is this? It’s a f–king farce so the stupid promotion can make a hundred million. Same as [Floyd] Mayweather fighting [Manny] Pacquiao later in his career.”

Paul weighed 227 pounds when he fought Mike Tyson in Nov. 2024, while the smallest he has fought at was 185 pounds against Nate Diaz in Aug. 2023.

Darren Till blasts Jake Paul for taking the Cédric Doumbé fight:“Jake Paul, he's a clear, clear juicehead. Look at him, mate, he's a fat juicehead. There's a fact for you.Cédric Doumbé's at 170 pounds… Jake Paul's 220, 225 pounds. You've gotta look past all the bullshit.… pic.twitter.com/5kJwkdirOD

Paul enters his Christmas Eve bout with Doumbé 12-2 after he was TKO’d by Anthony Joshua last year.

پوشش های بیشتری را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. دارن تیل از اینکه نبرد با جیک پل را دریافت نکرده است خشمگین است. پس از گمانه زنی ها و حتی تایید ادعایی مدیر عامل شرکت Most Valuable Promotions Nakisa Bidarian مبنی بر اینکه او در رقابت برای حریف بعدی پل بود، تیل پس از اینکه برای مبارزه با هلوانی در مصاحبه ای با آرییل هلوانی منتقل شد، بار را تخلیه کرد. تیل گفت: «ما روی قیمت به توافق رسیدیم و بدیهی است که قرار بود در 24 دسامبر در دبی، جایی که من زندگی می کنم، باشد. "من در دو هفته گذشته با مربیم در کمپ بودم؛ او را به بیرون پرواز دادم. آماده شدن در هفت هفته دیگر... از هیچ جایی، این مبارزه اعلام می شود؛ این مبارزه بد با سدریک دومبه اعلام می شود." دومبه و پل قرار است در شب کریسمس در دبی در وزن رزمناو (200 پوند) با هم مبارزه کنند، اگرچه دومبه، که از سال 2015 بوکس نکرده است اما یک کیک بوکسور آراسته است، آخرین بار 30 ماه پیش با وزن 175 پوند مبارزه کرد. جیک احتمالاً فقط می‌خواهد ببیند که فک او در برابر کسی که در یک روز خوب 150 پوند وزن دارد چگونه است. این یک نمایش تقلبی است. همه کلاهبردار هستند. جیک کلاهبردار است نکیسا یک کلاهبرداری کوچک است. اتلاف وقتم نمی توان f-k داد. اگر می خواهی سال بعد با من بجنگی، سال بعد با من بجنگ. بنابراین من فقط 5000 پوند هدر دادم تا مربیم را به اینجا برسانم، اما همه چیز خوب است."
دومبه 5 فوت-8 با دستیابی 73 اینچ است، در حالی که پل 6 فوت-1 را با 76 اینچ اندازه می گیرد. تیل توضیح داد: "سدریک دومبه 170 پوند وزن دارد." جیک پل 220

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Nobody does Halloween quite like Heidi Klum. The supermodel has become synonymous with the spooky holiday over the course of nearly three decades, regularly subjecting herself to hours of makeup, prosthetics, body casts and fittings for the sake of a jaw-dropping costume. And each year, she strives to outdo herself.

“I don’t want to let my Halloween fans down because there are so many people who love creativity as much as I do and are jonesing to see what I do,” Klum told Page Six Style in 2019.

Below, we take a look back at the committed catwalker’s most iconic costumes from over the years — from gruesome severed hand to “Shrek” ogress to wiggling worm — all ranked from mundane to magnificent.

“I wanted to be Heidi, but a little bit more S&M,” the model told us of her first-ever Halloween party look, which featured a German dirndl with a punk twist. Spooky enough, but nothing compared to her over-the-top outfits to come.

The highlight of this Halloween look? The horse, of course — which Klum wasn’t sure how to ride. “[The NYPD] gave me one of the police horses and it was very nice. But I was still scared,” she said.

Klum donned fake boobs and drawn-on brows to transform into the beloved cartoon character. Boop-Oop-a-Doop!

This bloodthirsty look required some major DIY on Klum’s part. “I had help with the costume but didn’t have [pro] hair and makeup until 2011!” she told us, adding that she sewed together five wigs to create her character’s voluminous ‘do.

While not especially creative by Klum’s standards, this look wins extra points for the commitment involved: “I had to go to one of those medical-supply stores and get a big, heavy fake skeleton that doctors and nurses use to study with, and carry it on my back all night long,” she told us.

Paging Moira Rose! We’re sure the model ruffled a few feathers in this caw-some creation. “I had just given birth. I was like, ‘Black is slimming,’” Klum explained of her choice.

Klum made for one fine feline in this slinky, glittery getup. Sometimes, you’ve just gotta go the “sexy animal” route!

When the COVID-19 pandemic put the kibosh on her annual costume bash, Klum pivoted and instead filmed a short horror movie at home to celebrate her favorite holiday. In the flick, the supermodel’s kids are transformed into zombies, so she hides by disguising herself as a wooden wall, marbleized bedsheets and more. You’ve got to applaud her for getting creative during a global crisis.

With the pandemic still raging, Klum once again canceled her Halloween rager in favor of making another spooky movie. This one picks up where the last left off, with the catwalker rising from the grave after being killed by her undead kids. Hat tips to horror classics like “Psycho,” “The Shining” and “The Exorcist” abound.

While this colorful costume was rather culturally insensitive, there’s no denying the artistry involved. Klum told us the eight-armed look was “tricky” to achieve: “You have this heavy backpack with eight arms you lug around all night.”

While nine months pregnant, Klum got extra creative. “I thought, ‘What can I be that is big and safe for the baby and comfortable for me?’ We had to get a convertible because I couldn’t fit through car doors,” she recalled of this Biblical look.

Klum gilded every inch of herself for this costume, from her hair to her teeth to her décolletage.

Talk about impressive wingspan! Klum told us “it was very hard to see” in this look. “I had these plastic round eyes and behind that, the batteries for the lights.”

Klum took this glamorous look to the next level by covering her face in crystals.

Klum doused herself in purple glitter and even wore red contacts to complete her costume. We’re still not sure how she managed to walk on those stilts.

She flipped the script for this dramatic entrance, arriving with an army of blond lookalikes with identical measurements. Prosthetics were used to make the models’ faces match Klum’s — eerie!

In the first of two looks she’d wear that year, Klum monkeyed around with then-husband Seal. She told us these looks were especially complicated to create: “An ape has so many spots, all these little freckles, and then [prosthetics artist Mike Marino] had to glue all these little hairs onto the prosthetics.”

Klum spent nine hours in the makeup chair morphing into the mythological monster capable of turning humans to stone. Her scaly suit was topped with moving mechanical snakes, and the Halloween queen even sported a custom split snake tongue.

Arguably the most terrifying of Klum’s costumes, this gory, gruesome alien-slash-zombie getup might give you nightmares.

Just call her Heidi Plume! The supe transformed into a larger-than-life peacock with an assist from a flock of Cirque du Soleil performers, who formed her “feathers.”

“I need all my friends around me. I thought it would be fun to do a costume with a bunch of people … where we all make amazing formations,” she told Page Six Style on the red carpet.

It took Klum six hours to prep for the party — and her husband, Tom Kaulitz, even attended as a giant peacock egg.

The star paid tribute to Michael Jackson with this killer outfit, even rehearsing for four days to get her dance moves just right.

It’s not easy being green — Klum piled on the prosthetics for this awesome outfit, pulling up at her party in an onion carriage. Kaulitz, meanwhile, joined her dressed as the movie’s titular ogre.

Inspired by the “Body Worlds” exhibition, Klum shed her skin for this creepy costume, arriving on a gurney accompanied by a duo of doctors.

In perhaps her most elaborate prosthetic work to date, Heidi and Tom both transformed into different versions of E.T. from Steven Spielberg’s 1982 film, with the supermodel adding a wig, scarf and cap to her look. The couple’s faces were actually part of the character’s neck, with the enormous motorized head sitting on top of their own. She had a glowing finger and working mouth and eyelids, adding to the spectacular nature of the costume.

For the first time ever, the supermodel wore an adult diaper on the red carpet. Now that’s commitment!

A true testament to the magic of makeup, this elderly look rendered Klum unrecognizable. The model told us the costume — her personal favorite so far — “was sparked by people telling me, ‘Wow, you’re 40 now, how are you feeling with being old in [the modeling] industry?’”

Klum outdid herself in every way with this cartoon creation come to life. “I was looking up who is the most well-known sex symbol — and it’s Jessica Rabbit,” recalled Klum. “I said, ‘Perfect.’ What man doesn’t want Jessica Rabbit? I wanted plus-plus everything: boots, butt, lips. Everyone was grabbing my boobs and butt because they knew they were fake.”

You’ve got to hand it to her: That’s one scary good Halloween look. Klum showed up at her annual bash as a supersized replica of her own hand, complete with her unique green alexandrite engagement ring, wedding band and “Tom” finger tattoo. A bloody wrist (with gore galore) and matching crimson manicure finished things off.

It took more than 10 hours to transform Klum into a giant worm — and she was quite the catch for Kaulitz, who dressed up as a fisherman who hooked her to his line.

At her party, Klum told reporters she considered the creepy-crawly costume one of her “top ones,” because “it’s so unusual and so big in size and it’s weird” — but admitted it wasn’t the most mobile getup.

“It’s hard for me to move. I don’t really have arms or legs,” she said. “When I fall over I need someone to help me get back up. I’m kind of stuck in it, you know? It feels a little claustrophobic.”

As creative as it was creepy, this stands as Klum’s most iconic Halloween look to date.

New details have emerged surrounding the tragic death of Erin Benavides, the woman once accused of having an affair with Eva Longoria’s ex-husband Tony Parker.

According to a police report obtained by Page Six, investigators documented three firearms following the 54-year-old former prosecutor’s death at her Port Aransas, Texas, home on Oct. 14.

Police also documented multiple bullets found on the scene, according to the report.

The report further reveals that authorities received a call at approximately 7:08 p.m. from someone claiming that a woman had threatened to take her own life.

As previously reported, police arrived at Benavides’ home after a friend of her husband received an alarming text message from her.

Officers forced their way inside the residence, where they discovered Benavides with an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound.

Authorities previously said they found no evidence suggesting foul play.

In a statement to Page Six, the Port Aransas Police Department confirmed that officers responded to a welfare concern at approximately 7:34 p.m. on Oct. 14.

“Upon arrival, officers located a deceased female inside the residence with an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound. The Nueces County Medical Examiner’s Office responded to the scene and assumed responsibility for determining the official cause and manner of death.

“Based on the preliminary investigation, no foul play is suspected,” the statement continued. “However, this remains an active and ongoing investigation. The Port Aransas Police Department extends its condolences to the family and friends of Ms. Benavides.”

Benavides made headlines in 2010 after she was accused of having an emotional affair with Parker, who was married to the “Desperate Housewives” actress at the time.

Benavides, then married to Parker’s former San Antonio Spurs teammate Brent Barry, denied having an affair with the NBA star.

Longoria filed for divorce from Parker in November 2010, while Benavides and Barry also ended their marriage.

Benavides later pursued a career in law, serving as a prosecutor in Texas and working with organizations dedicated to helping vulnerable children.

She resigned from her position with the 38th Judicial District in August 2026, just two months before her death.

If you or someone you know is affected by any of the issues raised in this story, call the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 800-273-TALK (8255) or text Crisis Text Line at 741741.

news.originalContent:
Daily Caller Illustration; with Getty Images from Shannon Finney / Drew Angerer / John Moore

Democratic Virginia congressional candidate Beth Macy built her reputation in part by documenting the devastation of America’s opioid epidemic. But as she seeks a seat in Congress, critics are questioning whether her most famous work tells the full story of the crisis.

Macy’s 2018 bestseller, Dopesick, chronicled Purdue Pharma’s aggressive marketing of OxyContin and the devastating consequences of opioid addiction in American communities. The book was later adapted into an Emmy and Peabody-winning Hulu series, which Macy helped write and produce.

While Purdue Pharma’s role in fueling the epidemic is well documented, the television adaptation of Dopesick has faced academic criticism over its portrayal of the crisis, including a 2024 peer-reviewed study that questioned whether the series adequately captured the epidemic’s complexity.

The criticism comes as Macy, who is challenging Republican Rep. Ben Cline in Virginia’s 6th Congressional District, highlights her work on the opioid epidemic as part of her congressional campaign.

This weekend, I crossed the Potomac to travel to Winchester and Front Royal in Virginia’s 6th District to praise and boost Beth Macy @papergirlmacy, who is running strong against the shrinking MAGA base. The author of Dopesick and numerous important works on how right-wing politics is killing working-class communities across America, Beth has crossed over from simply documenting and analyzing right-wing destruction of American society to actively opposing it and organizing to replace it. She’s running a surging and exciting campaign for Congress. Sending Beth to the US House will be like sending other great authors in history to represent the people in government, thought leaders like Ben Franklin and Václav Havel. Another chance for a great breakthrough as organizing creates landslide conditions for change across America.

Macy’s campaign website credits Dopesick with helping shift America’s understanding of addiction. But pain-patient advocates argue that the national response to the epidemic has also overlooked Americans who depend on prescription opioids for legitimate medical treatment.

Pain-patient advocates contend that efforts to combat prescription opioid abuse have contributed to increasingly restrictive prescribing practices, leaving some patients with chronic or acute pain struggling to obtain relief even as the overdose epidemic has evolved. (RELATED: ‘Scum Of The Earth’: Victims Slam Sackler Family And Purdue Pharma)

Macy’s book examines how Purdue Pharma promoted OxyContin as less addictive despite its potential for abuse, misled doctors about its safety, incentivized high-dose prescriptions and prioritized profits over patients. She also explores how lax regulatory oversight, evolving medical standards emphasizing pain treatment, and widespread misinformation contributed to the expansion of opioid prescribing.

Anyone care to ask Beth Macy how she plans to undo the damage her novel Dopesick did to pain patients? For years, Americans were sold a very specific narrative about prescription opioids, reinforced by Beth Macy’s Dopesick. What deserves a thorough investigation is how some of the very people who helped shape and promote that narrative went on to benefit professionally and financially from opioid litigation, addiction treatment, and government policy. Andrew Kolodny, Anna Lembke, Art Van Zee, and Stephen Loyd all had roles in opioid litigation, addiction medicine, or prescribing policy. Macy herself received an award from the American Society of Addiction Medicine (ASAM), an addiction organization with financial relationships involving addiction-treatment pharmaceutical companies, including the manufacturer of the opioid, Suboxone. (Over 1600 lawsuits have been filed against the makers of Suboxone) If we’re going to follow the money behind prescription opioids, we need to follow the money behind the addiction-treatment industry. What’s particularly troubling is that Macy has acknowledged the harm being done to stable chronic-pain patients through forced tapers and restrictive prescribing policies. Beth, where is the comparable book, documentary, or national investigation into the patients who lost their physicians, their medications, their ability to function, and, in some cases, their lives? The Doctor Patient Forum has spent ten years documenting these stories. It’s time to investigate who profited from restricting them. (Andrew Kolodny (below) earned $500,000 for his expert testimony in a single opioid trial, and that was just ONE of multiple cases in which he served as an expert witness)

Purdue executives pleaded guilty to federal misbranding charges in 2007, and the company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in September 2019 amid thousands of opioid-related lawsuits. The Sackler family and Purdue subsequently agreed to a multibillion-dollar settlement aimed at addressing the damage caused by the epidemic. (RELATED: Purdue Pharma, Sacklers Reach $7.4 Billion National Opioid Settlement)

Macy has argued that accountability came too slowly and that resources for addiction treatment and recovery remained inadequate.

Her reporting helped bring national attention to the communities devastated by addiction, and the success of Dopesick made her a prominent voice in the national conversation over opioid abuse.

But the television adaptation has also drawn academic criticism over how it presented the causes of the epidemic.

A 2024 peer-reviewed analysis of Hulu’s adaptation of Dopesick published in the peer-reviewed journal PLOS One, for example, argued that the series oversimplified the opioid epidemic by placing much of the blame on Purdue Pharma and Richard Sackler while downplaying other contributing factors.

Although the researchers acknowledged that the series attempted to portray multiple dimensions of the opioid crisis, they concluded that it offered an overly simplified explanation by giving insufficient attention to other contributing factors, including failures within the health care and regulatory systems. Their analysis focused on the television adaptation rather than Macy’s original book and did not dispute Purdue’s documented misconduct.

For pain-patient advocates, the debate over how the crisis is portrayed has consequences beyond public perception. (RELATED: American Cartel: Drummer Disgusted Opioids Funded His Performance)

They argue that Dopesick and similar projects helped reinforce the idea that reducing the availability of prescription opioid pain medication was a necessary response to addiction and overdose — potentially contributing to policies and prescribing practices that went too far in restricting access for patients who legitimately need pain relief.

Despite those criticisms, the Purdue-centered narrative became a widely used framework for explaining the crisis, appearing in discussions surrounding non-opioid pain relievers in Congress, state legislative hearings, medical education, hospital physician training, academic medicine, addiction medicine and broader discussions surrounding prescribing practices and opioid policy.

The concerns are not limited to patient advocates. In 2022, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention updated its opioid prescribing guidelines, warning against inflexible prescribing restrictions and the rapid tapering or abrupt discontinuation of opioid medications.

The agency acknowledged that earlier recommendations had sometimes been misapplied, potentially exposing patients to serious harm. Its revised guidance emphasized individualized treatment decisions rather than rigid dosage limits.

The controversy underscores the challenges physicians face in treating pain and opioid addiction, as even medications intended to reduce overdose risks can carry significant side effects.

The Valley braved the rain to show support for Beth Macy! As Republicans in Washington drive up the cost of gas and groceries, @papergirlmacy knows families are struggling. She is focused on delivering for them. And she has what it takes to flip this seat. Get out and VOTE! 🗳️ https://t.co/N6QFNjNujJ

The debate comes against the backdrop of a broader history of opioid misuse. Historically, an estimated 75% to 80% of people who use heroin or illicit opioids reported first misusing prescription opioids, according to a National Institute on Drug Abuse (NIDA) research report.

However, the report notes that many obtained those drugs through diversion — from friends, family members or illicit markets — rather than through their own prescriptions.

As prescribing practices became more restrictive, advocates say some patients were left searching for alternatives as doctors moved away from traditional opioids, such as OxyContin.

One alternative is buprenorphine, an opioid medication used to treat both pain and opioid use disorder. The drug generally carries a lower risk of fatal overdose than traditional opioid painkillers such as oxycodone, making it an option for physicians seeking safer approaches to pain management.

But some formulations have also raised safety concerns. In 2022, the Food and Drug Administration warned that buprenorphine medications dissolved in the mouth, including Suboxone, had been associated with serious dental problems, including tooth decay and tooth loss.

The FDA emphasized that the medications’ benefits outweigh those risks, particularly for treating opioid use disorder, but required new warnings and additional guidance for patients and prescribers.

Suboxone’s manufacturers also face thousands of lawsuits alleging that its dissolvable film caused severe dental injuries and that patients were not adequately warned about the risks.

The backlash illustrates the complexities of treating pain and addiction as physicians weigh the benefits and potential harms of different opioid medications.

On #AxeFiles, Dopesick author Beth Macy, who’s has spent her life reporting on the erosion of small town/rural America, blisters Trump for wooing these communities w/a cocktail of false promises & hate. But she doesn’t let the Dems off the hook. Full pod👉https://t.co/285dJOCfPq https://t.co/zL4oBmBOPY

That perspective stands in contrast to the one at the center of Beth Macy’s Dopesick, which told the story of the opioid epidemic largely through the experiences of addiction, overdose, and communities devastated by drug abuse.

The debate raises questions about how she would approach the competing demands of addiction prevention and access to pain treatment as a federal lawmaker.

Macy has increasingly connected her reporting on addiction and economic hardship to broader political arguments about the struggles facing working-class communities.

In a post on X, Democratic Maryland Rep. Jamie Raskin appeared alongside Macy on Oct. 26, and described her as the “author of Dopesick and numerous important works on how right-wing politics is killing working-class communities across America.” (RELATED: Are The Trump Admin’s Efforts To Combat US Addiction Crisis Actually Working?)

As Macy campaigns on her experience documenting the opioid epidemic, her congressional bid raises questions about how she would approach the unintended consequences of the government’s response, particularly for patients who rely on prescription opioids for legitimate medical treatment.

The Daily Caller reached out to Macy’s congressional campaign for comment on those concerns but did not receive a response in time for publication.

news.originalContent:
Three New York City progressive Democrats are expected to win their midterm congressional races in Tuesday’s election.

In June, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani stood before a packed house of voters, rallying support for a new wave of candidates hoping to build on his progressive momentum by winning seats in Congress.

Inside Brooklyn’s historic Kings Theatre, the crowd answered chants of “Abolish ICE”, “Tax the rich” and “Free Palestine” with roaring applause, leaving little if any room for doubt about what the audience wanted from its politicians.

Within days, all three congressional hopefuls endorsed by Mamdani – Claire Valdez, Brad Lander and Darializa Avila Chevalier – had won their Democratic primaries, becoming the party’s candidates in the midterm election.

Lander, the former New York City comptroller, defeated Congressman Dan Goldman in a race in which Israel was the defining issue.

Avila Chevalier, a community organiser, unseated longtime Congressman Adriano Espaillat. Valdez, a lawmaker in the New York State Assembly and member of Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), won the contest to succeed retiring Congresswoman Nydia Velazquez.

Both Valdez and Avila Chevalier had the backing of New York City’s DSA chapter.

The candidates’ heavily Democratic districts mean they are likely to win congressional seats in Tuesday’s midterm elections. The June Democratic Party primaries effectively served as the main event for voters.

In the final hours before Tuesday’s midterm election, New York City – a place colloquially dubbed the city that never sleeps – is more politically sleepy, with canvassers a bit harder to find than they were in the final stretch before the primaries.

For the three progressive candidates, the past few months have been a test of how to turn bold campaign promises into policy they can actually deliver. The often slow minutiae of daily governance stand in stark contrast to buzzword-laden campaign slogans on the posters and signs galvanising their base of voters.

The three congressional candidates’ platforms overlap on issues like abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), ending US military aid to Israel and establishing a public healthcare system dubbed Medicare for All. But their paths into progressive politics differ.

Lander spent years in the New York City government, most recently as comptroller overseeing the city’s finances. After losing to Mamdani in the 2025 Democratic mayoral primary, he backed Mamdani in the election.

But Lander’s congressional campaign against incumbent Goldman brought him national attention, with Israel and Palestine emerging as the defining issue in the race to lead a district with one of the largest Jewish populations in the United States.

Lander has described Israel’s military campaign in Gaza as genocide and its occupation of Palestinian territory as apartheid. He also identifies as a Zionist who embraces pro-Palestinian activism, arguing that the positions are not mutually exclusive. Lander has long supported a two-state solution.

“It’s straightforward that some approach to more shared safety for Israelis and Palestinians and for Jews and Muslims and everybody else here makes more sense,” Lander said. “I also want to be able to listen across those divides and have thoughtful policy debates.”

Two weeks before Tuesday’s election, Israeli forces detained Lander in the occupied West Bank while he was volunteering to help with the olive harvest. Israeli authorities have since revoked his travel documents for a planned return visit.

“The main story I come home with is not the story of my detention or the revocation of my travel authorisation,” Lander said. “The main story that I come with is the ethnic cleansing of Palestinians in the West Bank, which I just saw with my own eyes.”

Lander has also long called for ICE to be abolished, including during President Donald Trump’s first term in office.

Avila Chevalier’s political rise was similarly shaped by immigration and Palestinian rights, though she has taken a more uncompromising approach.

After interning at a youth organisation in Nablus in the occupied West Bank in 2014, she returned to the US and became an advocate for Palestinian communities.

Her “Babies Not Bombs” platform calls for redirecting military spending, including aid to Israel, towards domestic priorities such as childcare and healthcare.

“It’s important for us to see our budgets as moral documents,” Avila Chevalier told Al Jazeera. “Our resources should be going towards the things that make our lives dignified and make our communities thrive – not towards war, not towards ICE or things that are harming our communities.”

Valdez, meanwhile, came to progressive politics through the labour movement. A former union-organiser-turned-state-assemblymember, she supports stronger labour protections, including federal legislation such as the Protecting the Right to Organize (PRO) Act to make union organising easier.

Valdez also backs national rent control and a government-run healthcare system to provide wider healthcare access than the country’s private-sector insurance model.

“Public programmes and entitlements have been under attack by the right,” Valdez told Al Jazeera as she exited a polling location in her district on the first day of early voting. “I think not just clawing those back but really advancing a vision for what those things should be will be top priorities.”

Abolishing ICE and ending military aid to Israel are lofty, ambitious goals, and neither is likely to be achieved without navigating competing interests in Congress and the White House. With the balance of congressional power potentially shifting towards Democrats in the midterms, the newcomers will have to decide which priorities to pursue first.

That means looking for more immediate wins comparable to Mamdani’s move to fill 200,000 potholes when he took office as mayor, according to progressive political strategist Nomiki Konst.

“[Get] on the same page about an issue that we all agree on and leverage that in the Democratic Congress because there’s no better time than the beginning,” Konst told Al Jazeera.

For Lander, one such measure is banning members of Congress from trading individual stocks.

“Maybe that restores a little bit of trust,” Lander said. “People say that’s gross that members of Congress trade stocks. At least this new Congress is doing something, you know, to show me they’re not just all in it for themselves.”

Lander also sees an opportunity to restore enhanced government subsidies that expired at the end of 2025, raising premiums for many people who buy their private-sector insurance plans individually.

“We can say we’re not going to pass a budget that doesn’t do that and force Republicans to vote one way or the other and see what Trump does,” Lander said.

For Avila Chevalier, an early priority would be her “Babies Not Bombs” agenda, redirecting funding towards domestic needs. Valdez wants to pass the PRO Act.

The three would not be the first progressive New Yorkers to enter Congress promising major change.

Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez won her legislative seat in 2018 by defeating longtime incumbent Joe Crowley. Since then, she has occasionally worked with Republicans on shared priorities.

In 2025, Ocasio-Cortez introduced legislation with Republican Representative Anna Paulina Luna of Florida to cap credit card interest rates at 10 percent, echoing a proposal from Senator Bernie Sanders of Vermont and Republican Senator Josh Hawley of Missouri.

The question, Konst says, is whether Mamdani’s endorsed candidates can turn ideological commitments into legislative results. Doing so will require compromise, including setting aside some priorities to advance others.

Avila Chevalier is under the microscope after calling for New York City Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch to resign over a man being shot in his car by ICE while his child was in the backseat. Avila Chevalier said she was later shoved to the ground by New York City police officers during protests following the shooting.

Mamdani reportedly appointed Tisch on the recommendation of Governor Kathy Hochul, whose support was important to Mamdani’s mayoral campaign. An Atlantic magazine report suggested that her endorsement of Mamdani, whose more progressive platform included universal childcare and government-operated grocery stores, hinged on Tisch’s appointment.

“Everybody wants to have their agenda passed, right? I think being really thoughtful about when to hold fire, when to fire, when to be bold, when to hold back, and when to say what you feel so you’ll get the most support,” Konst said.

But Avila Chevalier said she is willing to work with anyone to advance her priorities.

“There is always something that two people can agree on. And that’s where I plan on starting because I think organising is about meeting people where they’re at,” Avila Chevalier said.

“There are so many folks who really want to see healthcare transformed in this country, who really want to see a moratorium on data [centres]. That is a bipartisan issue for so many.”

news.originalContent:
The United Nations ends its peacekeeping mission in the disputed territory.

It’s one of Africa’s longest-running conflicts.

The dispute over the territory of Western Sahara started more than 50 years ago. It began with the end of Spanish colonial rule in the region.

Since then, both Morocco and the Polisario Front have claimed the Western Sahara.

In the 1990s, the United Nations tried to reach a settlement, and deployed a peacekeeping mission to the region.

Last week, that effort ended when Russia and the United States blocked proposals to extend the mission’s mandate.

So, could this development lead to renewed fighting?

Samir Bennis – Political analyst and author of the book The Self-Determination Delusion: How Activist Scholars and Journalists Have Hijacked the Western Sahara Case

Irene Fernandez-Molina – Senior lecturer in International Relations at the University of Exeter in the United Kingdom and author of the book Moroccan Foreign Policy under Mohammed VI, 1999-2014

Mahjoub Mleiha –  Advocacy head of Collective of Sahrawi Human Rights Defenders (CODESA)
news.content:
سازمان ملل به ماموریت حفظ صلح خود در منطقه مورد مناقشه پایان می دهد. این یکی از طولانی ترین درگیری های آفریقا است. اختلاف بر سر قلمرو صحرای غربی بیش از 50 سال پیش آغاز شد. با پایان حکومت استعماری اسپانیا در منطقه آغاز شد. از آن زمان، هم مراکش و هم جبهه پولیساریو ادعای صحرای غربی را داشتند. در دهه 1990، سازمان ملل متحد تلاش کرد به یک توافق دست یابد و یک ماموریت حافظ صلح را در منطقه مستقر کرد. هفته گذشته، این تلاش زمانی به پایان رسید که روسیه و ایالات متحده پیشنهادات برای تمدید ماموریت این ماموریت را مسدود کردند. بنابراین، آیا این پیشرفت می تواند به جنگ مجدد منجر شود؟ پرونده صحرای غربی را ربود ایرنه فرناندز-مولینا – مدرس ارشد روابط بین الملل در دانشگاه اکستر انگلستان و نویسنده کتاب سیاست خارجی مراکش تحت نظر محمد ششم، 1999-2014

news.originalContent:
South Africa loses duty-free access under AGOA, impacting $1.7bn worth of exports, including cars and farm products.

The United States has said it will suspend South Africa and Rwanda from duty-free trade benefits under the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA), effective January 1, 2027.

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said Monday that both countries had failed to meet AGOA’s eligibility criteria. South Africa has been the largest beneficiary of the programme, exporting about $1.7bn worth of goods to the US under AGOA in 2025.

“President Trump found that the governments of Rwanda and South Africa are engaging in practices that are inconsistent with AGOA’s eligibility criteria,” Greer said in a statement.

There was no immediate response from either country.

AGOA beneficiaries are expected to meet eligibility requirements covering progress towards market-based economies, good governance and the elimination of barriers to US trade and investment, with Washington reviewing their eligibility annually.

Washington highlighted trade barriers, rule of law and human rights as issues it is deeply concerned about in Rwanda, which was also suspended in 2018.

With regard to South Africa, Washington said it was concerned by barriers to US trade and investment, corruption and threats to US national security and foreign policy interests.

President Donald Trump’s administration has cracked down on South Africa for what Trump says is its persecution of white people. South Africa’s government says this is a falsehood spread by fringe groups.

The US has also taken issue with South Africa’s foreign policy, in particular the genocide case it brought against Israel at the International Court of Justice. Israel denies genocide allegations.

South Africa’s Department of Trade, Industry and Competition said last week it was prepared for a negative outcome from the AGOA eligibility review and that it remained open to dialogue with the US. Exports under AGOA make up only about 10 percent of the country’s total exports to the US and 1 percent of its total global exports, it noted.

South African President Cyril Ramaphosa had also said in recent weeks that his country must prepare for being cut out of the programme, and that it was already seeking new markets and signing new trade deals with other partners such as China.

South Africa’s main exports to the US include precious stones and metals, motor vehicles, iron and steel. Its exports under AGOA are mainly motor vehicles and parts, as well as farm products and wine.

Rwanda’s main exports to the United States include coffee, tea and minerals.
news.content: آفریقای جنوبی دسترسی معاف از گمرک را تحت AGOA از دست می دهد و بر صادرات به ارزش 1.7 میلیارد دلار از جمله خودروها و محصولات کشاورزی تأثیر می گذارد. ایالات متحده اعلام کرده است که آفریقای جنوبی و رواندا را از مزایای تجارت معاف از گمرک تحت قانون رشد و فرصت آفریقا (AGOA) معلق خواهد کرد. معیارهای واجد شرایط بودن آفریقای جنوبی بزرگترین ذینفع از این برنامه بوده است و حدود 1.7 میلیارد دلار کالا به ایالات متحده تحت AGOA در سال 2025 صادر کرده است. گریر در بیانیه ای گفت: "رئیس جمهور ترامپ دریافت که دولت های رواندا و آفریقای جنوبی در حال انجام اقداماتی هستند که با معیارهای واجد شرایط بودن AGOA سازگار نیست." انتظار می رود که ذینفعان AGOA الزامات واجد شرایط بودن را پوشش دهند که شامل پیشرفت به سمت اقتصادهای مبتنی بر بازار، حکمرانی خوب و از بین بردن موانع تجارت و سرمایه گذاری ایالات متحده می شود و واشنگتن سالانه صلاحیت آنها را بررسی می کند. واشنگتن موانع تجاری، حاکمیت قانون و حقوق بشر را به عنوان موضوعاتی که در رواندا عمیقاً نگران آن است، برجسته کرد. در رابطه با آفریقای جنوبی، واشنگتن گفت که نگران موانع تجارت و سرمایه گذاری ایالات متحده، فساد و تهدیدات امنیت ملی و منافع سیاست خارجی ایالات متحده است. دولت دونالد ترامپ، رئیس جمهور آمریکا، آفریقای جنوبی را به دلیل آنچه ترامپ می گوید آزار و اذیت سفیدپوستان است، سرکوب کرده است. جنوب آف

news.originalContent:
Opposition figures arrested and disappeared since President Hakainde Hichilema claimed August victory.

Human Rights Watch (HRW) has called on Zambia’s authorities to halt the vicious clampdown on the political opposition that was launched following President Hakainde Hichilema’s victory in disputed elections in August.

The rights group demanded in a report released on Sunday that the authorities put a stop to the intensifying crackdown.

It accused Zambia’s government of silencing government critics, with several members of the opposition, as well as journalists and lawyers, arrested and some having disappeared in recent months.

“The post-election climate of intimidation, harassment, and repression has had a chilling effect on civic and political organizations, particularly on dissenting voices,” HRW said.

The group said that Zambian police and military “forcibly disappeared, arbitrarily detained, beat, and threatened opposition members and supporters as well as lawyers, journalists, and government critics in the days before and after general elections in August 2026”.

“Zambia’s government should break this dangerous cycle of repression,” added Ashwanee Budoo-Scholtz, deputy Africa director at HRW.

“The authorities should immediately halt the ongoing post-election crackdown, allow access to lawyers and provide medical care for those in detention, release everyone arbitrarily detained, and ensure accountability for abuses by security forces.”

Hichilema was sworn in for a second term as Zambia’s president following his victory in August. Critics have insisted that the election was marred by vote rigging.

As he was inaugurated at the National Heroes Stadium in the Zambian capital, Lusaka, his main rival Brian Mundubile was in detention, accused of treason after claiming the opposition had won the election.

Police raided Mundubile’s home the day after the August 13 elections. A former cabinet member, Mutotwe Kafwaya, was shot and killed during the operation.

HRW called on the Zambian authorities to institute an independent, impartial and thorough investigation into the matter.

About a dozen other opposition figures who have questioned the election results have been arrested.

Meanwhile, authorities suddenly closed the country’s courts two weeks after the election, a move that Zambian police stated was an “intelligence-led and preventive measure”, without providing details.

HRW noted that the closure prevents the opposition from filing legal challenges against the vote.
news.content:
از زمانی که رئیس جمهور هاکاینده هیچیلما مدعی پیروزی در ماه اوت شد، چهره های اپوزیسیون دستگیر و ناپدید شدند. دیده بان حقوق بشر (HRW) از مقامات زامبیا خواسته است تا سرکوب شرورانه مخالفان سیاسی را که پس از پیروزی رئیس جمهور هاکاینده هیچیلما در انتخابات مورد مناقشه در ماه اوت آغاز شد، متوقف کنند. این سازمان دولت زامبیا را متهم کرد که منتقدان دولت را ساکت کرده است و چندین تن از اعضای اپوزیسیون، همچنین روزنامه نگاران و وکلا، دستگیر و برخی در ماه های اخیر ناپدید شده اند. دیده بان حقوق بشر گفت: «فضای ارعاب، آزار و اذیت و سرکوب پس از انتخابات، تأثیر وحشتناکی بر سازمان های مدنی و سیاسی، به ویژه بر صداهای مخالف داشته است». این گروه گفت که پلیس و ارتش زامبیا «به زور اعضای و حامیان اپوزیسیون و همچنین وکلا، روزنامه نگاران و منتقدان دولت را در روزهای قبل و بعد از انتخابات عمومی در اوت 2026 ناپدید، خودسرانه بازداشت، ضرب و شتم و تهدید کردند». "مقامات باید فورا سرکوب جاری پس از انتخابات را متوقف کنند، اجازه دسترسی به وکلا و ارائه مراقبت های پزشکی را برای افراد بازداشت شده فراهم کنند، همه افرادی که خودسرانه بازداشت شده اند را آزاد کنند و از پاسخگویی در مورد سوء استفاده های نیروهای امنیتی اطمینان حاصل کنند."

news.originalContent:
A closely watched, neck-and-neck Senate race in the heart of the country quickly turned into a battle over Big Tech, its role in the state’s economy, and its immense influence in state and national politics. Fearing a populist backlash channeled by a newly empowered Democratic Party, the tech industry is spending big bucks to prevent a blue flip.

Ohio has become a major hub for AI and tech data centers, and tech and energy leaders have committed tens of billions of dollars to the state, including massive multi-billion-dollar investments by Amazon and Google. Hundreds of data centers are operating or planned as of early November, with central Ohio, particularly around the Columbus region, hosting over 100 facilities. It is one of the densest data center corridors in the country. (RELATED: Seems Like Every Single Political Race Centers Around Single Issue)
news.content: مسابقه ای که از نزدیک تماشا می شد و گردن و گردن در قلب کشور بود، به سرعت به نبردی بر سر فناوری بزرگ، نقش آن در اقتصاد ایالت و نفوذ بسیار زیاد آن در سیاست ایالتی و ملی تبدیل شد. صنعت فناوری از ترس واکنش پوپولیستی که توسط یک حزب تازه قدرت یافته دموکرات هدایت می شود، دلارهای زیادی را برای جلوگیری از تلنگر آبی هزینه می کند. اوهایو به مرکز اصلی هوش مصنوعی و مراکز داده فناوری تبدیل شده است و رهبران فناوری و انرژی ده ها میلیارد دلار به این ایالت متعهد شده اند، از جمله سرمایه گذاری های عظیم چند میلیارد دلاری آمازون و گوگل. صدها مرکز داده از اوایل نوامبر در حال فعالیت یا برنامه ریزی هستند، با مرکز اوهایو، به ویژه در اطراف منطقه کلمبوس، میزبان بیش از 100 تسهیلات. این یکی از متراکم ترین راهروهای مرکز داده در کشور است. پیروزی احتمالی دموکرات‌ها در کنگره می‌تواند موانع عمده‌ای در مسیر اجرای برنامه‌های کاخ سفید ایجاد کند، مسیر تصمیم‌گیری‌های کلان را به چالش بکشد و با فعال‌سازی اهرم‌های نظارتی و آغاز تحقیقات پارلمانی، چالش‌های سیاسی گسترده‌ای را برای دولت دونالد ترامپ در دو سال پایانی ریاست‌جمهوری‌اش رقم بزند.
